thread:
emma_cs: Heads up — ParcelBee (dedicated eu-west-2) opened an escalation: intermittent 429s + p99 latency spikes since ~09:12 UTC. They report their traffic was steady but the pool keeps scaling up/down every ~3m and causing transient throttles. Ticket #12345.

matt_oncall: looking now. any repro steps from support?

rebecca_support: customer pasted this timeline: 09:11:50 heavy request burst, 09:12:20 pool scales +2, 09:14:00 instances removed, 09:15:30 429s for 20–40s, repeats. They included a curl used to hit our endpoint (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/parcelbee/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"<long chat turn repeated>", "max_tokens":1024}'
```

infra-bot: autoscaler event: scale_up at 2024-11-03T09:12:21Z (+2), scale_down at 2024-11-03T09:14:05Z (-2). Cooldown=120s configured on that pool.

nick_sre: cooldown set to 120s but the pattern looks like pendulum — metrics bouncing past thresholds repeatedly. Possible causes: noisy neighbor spike that triggers vertical autoscale, or our queue_length metric is jittery because of request batching + client burstiness.

jin_runtime: can we see the per-instance CPU/GPU and queue_length time series? also check if KV cache flushes happened (that can cause transient CPU).

matt_oncall: pulling logs now. snippet from controller: 

```
[09:12:20] metric_queue_length=18 threshold=12 -> scale_up
[09:12:21] provision request queued -> provisioning start
[09:12:40] new node ready -> traffic shift
[09:13:50] metric_queue_length drops to 3 -> scale_down scheduled
[09:14:05] scale_down executed -> terminated 2 nodes
[09:14:10] error: allocate failed for 1 request -> 429 returned
```

rebecca_support: customer says their traffic profile is fairly flat; no known bursts. They run a nightly batch at 03:00 UTC but that shouldn't hit 09:12.

nick_sre: theory: short-term burst of few dozen parallel requests plus current batching settings pushed queue metric over threshold. Our scale_down is too aggressive — takes effect while new nodes are still warming or before request tails finish. We should increase 'stable_window' or add smoothing/derivative filter.

jin_runtime: agree. propose quick mitigation: bump cooldown to 300s for that pool and enable exponential moving average (EMA) smoothing on queue_length with alpha=0.2. Also set min_ready_instances=2 extra buffer.

matt_oncall: I can push a temp policy change if we agree. Any objections?

kevin_billing: FYI customer is on Reserved Dedicated plan — we can change config without billing impact.

rebecca_support: customer asked for reproducible steps in case we need to test from their side. Suggested steps I sent:
1) send 40 parallel requests over 15s to the dedicated endpoint using their key
2) wait 90s, repeat 3x
3) collect 429s/p95 logs and share.

nick_sre: additional diagnostics to collect before config change:
- per-instance gpu_util, cpu, oom logs
- controller autoscaler alerts (pre/post)
- per-request latency and which node handled it
- any cache flush logs from runtime

matt_oncall: applying temp change to pool parcelbee-eu2: cooldown=300s, enable EMA smoothing (alpha=0.2), min_ready_instances += 2. Will monitor for 30m.

infra-bot: policy_update applied by matt_oncall at 2024-11-03T09:45:10Z: {cooldown:300, ema_alpha:0.2, min_ready:+2}

jin_runtime: while we monitor, let's also check whether prefetch/warmup eviction is happening — if new nodes aren't bringing KV cache up then initial requests might be slow and trigger scale again. If so, warmup-hook to prefetch common prefixes could help.

rebecca_support: I told ParcelBee support we'll keep them posted and asked for their traffic runbook and any SDK retry behavior.

matt_oncall: initial 30min looks promising — no 429s in last 12m, p95 down. leaving policy in place and will reassess tomorrow.

nick_sre: follow-ups: (a) add a hysteresis test to our autoscaler test-suite (b) evaluate whether queue_length sampling interval needs to be thicker (20s -> 60s) for dedicated pools with batching (c) add annotation to pool config to prevent aggressive scale_down if avg_latency > X ms.

rebecca_support: customer thanks the team, will update ticket if they see recurrence. :thumbsup:

matt_oncall: closing loop for now. if anyone wants to run repro load against staging dedicated to validate, ping me and I'll provide creds.
